about: The smoke of the cigarette the player smokes on the balcony on launch day, a thin wisp rising off the lit end all the time it burns, and the breath of a drag let out ahead of the face, slowing, spreading, rising and thinning away. Both are let go into the world rather than carried with the head. The player's eye is the scene record's balcony camera, so both are hung off it, at the lips and the lit end measured on a face and a cigarette; the cigarette itself, the player's own, is not on the stage. Every shape, speed and count is measured on real footage (the footage block), the spots on a face's and a cigarette's measures, the colour on the footage's pixels and the breaths' spacing on smokers' measured puffing. Real footage checked before: exhaled cigarette smoke leaves the lips as a dense stream that slows within a few tens of centimetres and billows, and a resting cigarette's smoke rises as one thin laminar thread that breaks into curls (the owner's rule: start from footage, many fine cards tied to the world).

effects.name: wisp
effects.from: footage: commons-Cigarettesmoke.JPG, commons-Still_smoking_(2329760820).jpg, commons-Incense_stick.JPG (one thin thread off the lit end, straight for 4 to 10 cm, then folding into curls and sheets that widen at 15 to 35 degrees either side, one connected veil seen at least 22 cm up and never loose blobs: 3,000 fine cards a 3 s life, rising at 0.12 to 0.2 m/s and slowly growing to about 5 cm, each faint so many overlap into the thread); the lit end at the lips 66 mm under the eye (the pupil to the mouth's opening, 65.52 plus or minus 5.28 mm over 500 adults: dovepress CCIDE, 'An anthropometric study to evaluate the correlation between the occlusal vertical dimension and length of the thumb', https://www.dovepress.com/an-anthropometric-study-to-evaluate-the-correlation-between-the-occlus-peer-reviewed-fulltext-article-CCIDE) and 27 mm ahead of it (measured on commons-Exhaling_cloud_of_cigarette_smoke_(50652653823).png against its head's 19.5 cm length) plus a king size cigarette's 84 mm (https://eastern-tobacco.com/cigarette-sizes-and-dimensions-complete-format-guide/) less the 11 mm smokers hold in their lips (10.6 and 11.0 mm on average over 2,232 butts' saliva marks: 'Mouth Insertion Depths in Canadian Smokers', https://reference-global.com/article/10.2478/cttr-2013-0673), held level and straight ahead (no footage here gives a held cigarette's angle: the record's own choice); the colour #e5e6e6, neutral: the mean of the brightest 5% of the unclipped smoke pixels of commons-Cigarettesmoke.JPG under a warm lamp (#e0dad5) and commons-Exhaling_cloud_of_cigarette_smoke_(50652653823).png in sunlight (#eaf3f7), smoke taking its light's colour; turbulence, its fading and the drift into the world set so the bake meets the footage block's checks (one veil, its half angle, its reach)

effects.name: breath
effects.from: footage: commons-Exhaling_cloud_of_cigarette_smoke_(50652653823).png, doi-10.1371/journal.pone.0059970, doi-10.1111/j.1600-0668.2009.00623.x, pmc-PMC7111220 (a breath of smoke leaving the lips about level at up to 1.3 m/s, spreading 15 to 25 degrees either side, slowing within 0.6 to 2.5 s and billowing 0.2 to 0.8 m ahead of the mouth, barely rising: 4,000 fine cards let out over 1.2 s, slowed by 1.3 to 1.8 m/s/s, growing to about 0.15 m as they spread); let out at the lips 66 mm under the eye (the pupil to the mouth's opening, 65.52 plus or minus 5.28 mm over 500 adults: dovepress CCIDE, 'An anthropometric study to evaluate the correlation between the occlusal vertical dimension and length of the thumb', https://www.dovepress.com/an-anthropometric-study-to-evaluate-the-correlation-between-the-occlus-peer-reviewed-fulltext-article-CCIDE) and 27 mm ahead of it (measured on commons-Exhaling_cloud_of_cigarette_smoke_(50652653823).png against its head's 19.5 cm length); the colour #e5e6e6, neutral: the mean of the brightest 5% of the unclipped smoke pixels of commons-Cigarettesmoke.JPG under a warm lamp (#e0dad5) and commons-Exhaling_cloud_of_cigarette_smoke_(50652653823).png in sunlight (#eaf3f7), smoke taking its light's colour; a breath every 20 s: smokers' mean time between puffs, 19.9 s in the laboratory (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/14577984) and 32.5 s over a week of their own days (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7277227/), puffs of 1.5 to 2 s, the bake's loop the shorter; the first let out 0.8 s into the stage (the stage's own: its pictures at 2 s see it 1.2 s out, inside the 0.5 to 2.5 s the schlieren tracked a breath); turbulence, its fading and the drift into the world set so the bake meets the footage block's checks (one veil, its half angle, its reach)

views.name: balcony-smoke

views.name: balcony-smoke-side
views.from: the stage's own: from just past the balcony rail, 3 m off the player's eye, looking back at where the smoke is let out (the breath is let out at the lips, under the eye, so the eye's own camera barely sees it)

rides_nothing: the smoke hangs off the player's eye (the balcony camera), as the game hangs the cigarette off the player's camera; the player is not on the stage and the smoke is let go into the world
no_light: smoke gives off no light of its own; the flat's lamps and the city light it

footage.how: Measured on each photograph's pixels against a thing of known size in it (the cigarette's width, a head's length), or read off a paper's text. A plume running off the frame bounds a measure on one side only (null). The seconds are the stage's: the breath is let out 0.8 s into each 20 s, and the balcony pictures are taken 1.2 s after it.

commons-Cigarettesmoke.JPG.what: a hand-held lit cigarette, its smoke against a plain wall in still indoor air (Wikimedia Commons)
commons-Cigarettesmoke.JPG.measured: measured on its pixels against the cigarette's 7.8 mm width (15 px of 900): clear for about 1.5 cm over the ember, one straight thread about 6.8 cm long, then folding into sheets and curls; the plume at least 22 cm over the tip before the frame's edge, widening at 25 to 35 degrees either side above the break; one connected veil, no loose blobs

commons-Still_smoking_(2329760820).jpg.what: a cigarette butt in an ashtray, a thin thread of smoke (Wikimedia Commons)
commons-Still_smoking_(2329760820).jpg.measured: measured against the butt's 7.8 mm width (55 px): one faint thread 6.5 cm up to the frame's top, still unbroken, meandering from 3.5 cm up

commons-Incense_stick.JPG.what: an incense stick's smoke on black, the same kind of plume (Wikimedia Commons)
commons-Incense_stick.JPG.measured: measured against the stick (3 to 5 mm across): smooth for about 4 to 6 cm, then curling, seen 10 to 17 cm up, fanning out at about 28 degrees either side; folded sheets, no blobs

commons-Exhaling_cloud_of_cigarette_smok.what: a man in profile breathing out cigarette smoke outdoors (Wikimedia Commons)
commons-Exhaling_cloud_of_cigarette_smok.measured: measured against the head's length (about 19.5 cm, an adult's typical): the dense core about 8 cm from the lips, the whole cloud about 0.20 m ahead and 0.18 m tall, opening 20 to 25 degrees either side on the mean, its middle 1.5 cm over the mouth; soft and billowing, no loose blobs

doi-10.1371/journal.pone.0059970.what: Tang et al. 2013, schlieren of human breathing (PLoS ONE), 20 people
doi-10.1371/journal.pone.0059970.measured: read: breathing out of the mouth goes at most 0.8 m at up to 1.3 m/s, mainly level, not lifted by its warmth within the first metre, tracked for 0.5 to 2.5 s

doi-10.1111/j.1600-0668.2009.00623.x.what: Gupta, Lin and Chen 2010, the air breathed out in breathing and talking (Indoor Air)
doi-10.1111/j.1600-0668.2009.00623.x.measured: read: the mouth's jet leaves about level, spreading 30 degrees seen from the side (about 15 either side; 27 to 34 over four people)

pmc-PMC7111220.what: Xu et al. 2017, schlieren and anemometer of breathing out (Building and Environment)
pmc-PMC7111220.measured: read: standing, mouth only, spreading 36 plus or minus 6 degrees (about 18 either side); under 0.1 m/s by 0.4 m out
